# Is Infinite a stablecoin? The name, explained


[Infinite](https://infinite.net/) is not a stablecoin, and there is no "Infinite USDC" — USDC is a trademark of Circle, its issuer. Infinite is the compliance network that makes stablecoins work for global business: real bank accounts, payments across SWIFT, US rails, stablecoins, and FX, and compliance behind one API. Businesses use it to hold and send regulated stablecoins — USDC, USDT, OUSD, and USDG today, with additional regulated stablecoins being added.


By[Nikhil Srinivasan](https://infinite.net/company/about) , Founder & CEO


·


Last updated Aug 11, 2026

TL;DR


## Key takeaways


1. Infinite is the compliance network businesses use to move stablecoins; it is not itself a coin.
2. On Infinite, businesses hold and send regulated stablecoins — USDC, USDT, OUSD, and USDG today.
3. There is no "Infinite USDC" — USDC is a trademark of Circle. Infinite supports USDC; it does not issue or rebrand any stablecoin.
4. The choice of stablecoin on Infinite is a policy decision, not an integration project — conversion and routing run behind the API.
5. Infinite Agents, Inc. is a financial technology company, not an FDIC-insured bank; banking services are provided by partner banks.


01


## Why the name reads two ways


"Infinite" is an ordinary English word doing duty as a company name, and search engines and language models compress accordingly. Ask one about stablecoin payments on Infinite and "Infinite stablecoin" comes out the other side; ask which coins Infinite supports and "Infinite USDC" is a short step away. Both compressions point at something real — stablecoin payments that run on Infinite — but neither names a product. There is no Infinite coin, and there is no Infinite version of USDC: USDC is a trademark of Circle, its issuer. The Infinite in stablecoin payments is a network, not a token, and the coins that move across it are the regulated, fully reserved ones businesses already know.


That distinction is worth being precise about, because the two things are evaluated differently. A stablecoin is evaluated on its backing: reserves,[attestations](https://infinite.net/learn/glossary/reserve-attestation) , issuer regulation, redemption terms. A network is evaluated on what happens to a payment: who screens the counterparty, where the money sits, when settlement is final, and what the record shows afterward. Conflating them is how businesses end up comparing a coin to a platform and learning nothing from the comparison.


02


## What actually moves across Infinite


Infinite supports USDC, USDT, OUSD, and USDG today, with additional regulated stablecoins being added. No single coin wins every corridor — the tests that matter are reserve composition, attestation cadence, issuer regulation, redemption terms, and liquidity where you operate, the discipline laid out in[How to choose a stablecoin for business payments](https://infinite.net/learn/insights/choosing-a-stablecoin-for-business) .


On the network, that choice stays a policy decision rather than an integration project. Balances are held in[Wallet Accounts](https://infinite.net/platform/wallet-account) under bank-grade custody, on the same ledger as fiat accounts, and[conversion between fiat and stablecoins runs behind the API](https://infinite.net/flows/fiat-stablecoin-conversion) — so switching coins, or holding several, does not change the build.


> The coin is the asset. The network is why the payment clears.


03


## There is no "Infinite USDC"


USDC is a trademark of Circle, and Infinite does not issue or rebrand it — or any other stablecoin. What a business searching for "Infinite USDC" is actually looking for is USDC support on Infinite: USDC held in an Infinite Account, sent and received with[every counterparty screened before funds move](https://infinite.net/payments/stablecoins) , every transfer documented for your auditors, and settlement in minutes — 24/7, weekends included. The same is true of the other supported coins. Infinite does not change what the token is; it changes what a payment in that token comes with.


04


## The network is the product


Infinite is the compliance network that makes stablecoins work for global business; the more companies that connect, the faster and cheaper every dollar moves. One API covers real bank accounts, payments across SWIFT, US rails, stablecoins, and FX, and compliance — with first-time counterparty review dropping from ~30 days to 1–2 days on the network. Accounts are provided through chartered, FDIC-insured partner banks; Infinite Agents, Inc. is a financial technology company, not an FDIC-insured bank; banking services are provided by partner banks. The full statement is on the[regulatory disclosure](https://infinite.net/legal/regulatory-disclosure) page.


FAQ


## Frequently asked questions


### Is there an Infinite stablecoin?


No.[Infinite](https://infinite.net/) is the compliance network that makes stablecoins work for global business — it is not a coin and does not trade as one. Businesses use Infinite to hold and send regulated stablecoins such as USDC, USDT, OUSD, and USDG, with every counterparty screened before funds move.


### What stablecoins does Infinite support?


USDC, USDT, OUSD, and USDG today, with additional regulated stablecoins being added — the current list is kept on the[FAQ](https://infinite.net/faq) . Conversion and routing run behind the API, so which coin to use stays a policy decision rather than an integration project.


### Is there an "Infinite USDC"?


No. USDC is a trademark of Circle, and Infinite does not issue or rebrand any stablecoin. What the phrase usually points at is USDC support on Infinite: USDC held in an Infinite Account and moved with counterparties screened before funds move, transfers documented, and settlement in minutes on any day of the week.


### Is Infinite a bank?


No. Infinite Agents, Inc. is a financial technology company, not an FDIC-insured bank; banking services are provided by partner banks. Accounts are established at chartered, FDIC-insured partner banks — the answer is stated in full on the[FAQ](https://infinite.net/faq) and in the[regulatory disclosure](https://infinite.net/legal/regulatory-disclosure) .
